meta.title: The Dead
meta.author: James Joyce / interactive adaptation
meta.description: A restrained interactive adaptation of James Joyce's The Dead, following Gabriel Conroy through a winter gathering, a song, and the snow beyond the living and the dead.

cover.label: The Dead
cover.tagline: Snow was general all over Ireland.

ach_true_snow.title: Faintly Falling
ach_true_snow.description: You let the snow reach the living and the dead.

ach_jealous.title: The Warm Room
ach_jealous.description: You kept the room warm and narrow.

ach_glass.title: Glass Between
ach_glass.description: You heard the story through a pane.

ach_westward.title: Westward
ach_westward.description: You followed the night toward the west.

ach_voice.title: A Voice Under Rain
ach_voice.description: You listened until the song had a body.

ach_door.title: The Door Left Open
ach_door.description: You stepped out before the house could claim you.

ach_laughter.title: Bad Form
ach_laughter.description: You broke the tact that held the evening together.

ach_table.title: No Toast
ach_table.description: You left the table without its customary words.

ach_corridor.title: The Corridor
ach_corridor.description: You chose the corridor over the story.

ach_lily.title: A Bitter Reply
ach_lily.description: You noticed the wound under Lily's answer.

ach_ivors.title: West Briton
ach_ivors.description: You let the accusation remain in the room.

scene.name: Morkan House Hall
scene.description: The hall is bare and narrow. Above it the floorboards answer the dance with a dull stamping.
scene.arrival: The bell has hardly stopped shaking when Lily opens the door.

segments.text: Snow lies on your shoulders and on the toes of your goloshes. Lily, the caretaker's daughter, stands back to let Gretta pass toward the stairs.

segments.speaker: Lily
segments.text: Miss Kate and Miss Julia thought you were never coming.

choices.text: Answer brightly and scrape the snow from your shoes.
Keep your eyes on the stairs where Gretta has gone.
Say you should never have come out in such weather.

scene.name: Open Doorway
scene.description: The cold enters as if it had been waiting for an invitation.
scene.arrival: Your hand remains on the wet latch.

segments.text: Lily stares at you, uncertain whether she is permitted to laugh. From upstairs one of your aunts calls down your name.
Gretta's voice answers them before yours can. The little ceremony of welcome goes on without you.

choices.text: Step back into the snow.

scene.name: Little Pantry
scene.description: A gas flame makes the shelves and folded coats look paler than they are.
scene.arrival: Lily helps the stiff overcoat from your shoulders.

segments.text: The ceiling shakes with the dance. Lily folds your coat carefully, all service and hurry.
You remember her as a child on the lowest stair with a rag doll in her arms.

choices.text: Ask whether she is still at school.
Let the servant be a servant and say nothing more.

scene.name: Little Pantry
scene.description: A gas flame makes the shelves and folded coats look paler than they are.

segments.speaker: Lily
segments.text: I'm done schooling this year and more.
You hear yourself become genial, almost paternal.

choices.text: Joke that her wedding will be next.
Say only that Miss Kate depends upon her tonight.

scene.name: Little Pantry
scene.description: The room is too small for the answer that comes.

segments.speaker: Lily
segments.text: The men that is now is only all palaver and what they can get out of you.
The words strike your face before you have time to arrange one of your own.

choices.text: Push a coin into her hand and escape upstairs.
Murmur an apology, too low for the hallway to hear.

scene.name: Little Pantry
scene.description: The dance above continues without waiting for either of you.

segments.speaker: Lily
segments.text: They do be fussy, sir.
She says it without insolence. It is nearly gratitude, but not quite.

choices.text: Thank her and go up.

scene.name: Drawing Room Door
scene.description: Skirts sweep against the other side of the door. Men's heels clack out the measure.
scene.arrival: You wait until the waltz should finish.

segments.text: You take the folded paper from your waistcoat pocket. Browning stands there among the headings, looking suddenly too high for the room.
The evening must be managed. So must your tone.

choices.text: Keep the Browning line. They may rise to it.
Resolve to speak simply for your aunts.
Fold the paper away. You will not perform for them tonight.

scene.name: Landing
scene.description: Kate and Julia move in small, anxious circles around Gretta and the stairs.

segments.speaker: Gretta
segments.text: The next thing he'll buy me will be a diving suit.
The aunts laugh. You laugh too, but your hand goes to your tie.

choices.text: Defend the word. Everyone wears them on the continent.
Let Gretta have the joke.

scene.name: Stairs
scene.description: The banisters carry every laugh and whisper.

segments.speaker: Aunt Kate
segments.text: Slip down, Gabriel, like a good fellow, and see if he's all right.
From below comes Freddy Malins' laugh, already apologizing for itself.

choices.text: Pilot him upstairs with cheerful firmness.
Warn him sharply where the young ladies can hear.

scene.name: Landing
scene.description: The dance has stopped, but no one has announced it.

segments.text: Freddy's face remains red, yet the laugh goes out of it. Aunt Kate looks at you as if you had dropped a dish.
The house continues, but no longer with the same confidence.

choices.text: Stand in the silence you have made.

scene.name: Drawing Room
scene.description: The chandelier glitters on the polished floor; old pictures hang above the piano.
scene.arrival: You return to the drawing room as Mary Jane begins again.

segments.text: Your eyes leave the music and settle on the wool-work picture, the dead princes, then on your mother's photograph.
A phrase of hers returns: country cute. It had not been true of Gretta.

choices.text: Let the memory pass before it can rankle.
Hold the old slight against your mother and the room.

scene.name: Dance Floor
scene.description: The figures of the lancers gather and part with exact little bows.

segments.speaker: Miss Ivors
segments.text: I have a crow to pluck with you.
Her Irish brooch catches the light as plainly as an accusation.

choices.text: Smile and ask what offence you have committed.
Brace yourself before she has named it.

scene.name: Dance Floor
scene.description: The other dancers are near enough to hear a word if it is sharpened.

segments.speaker: Miss Ivors
segments.text: To say you'd write for a paper like that. I didn't think you were a West Briton.
The phrase enters the figure of the dance and will not leave it.

choices.text: Say literature is above politics, but say it lightly.
Tell her she has no right to make you ridiculous.
Ask what she thinks you have betrayed.

scene.name: Dance Floor
scene.description: Hands meet and part; the question remains when the figure changes.

segments.speaker: Miss Ivors
segments.text: Will you come for an excursion to the Aran Isles this summer?
She says it would be splendid for Gretta too. Connacht is brought into the room as if it had been waiting outside.

choices.text: Say you have arranged for France or Belgium.
Admit that Gretta might like to see Galway again.

scene.name: Dance Floor
scene.description: Neighbours have begun to listen.

segments.speaker: Miss Ivors
segments.text: And haven't you your own land to visit?
Heat comes into your forehead before the answer is ready.

choices.text: Retort that you are sick of your own country.
Let the dance carry the question away unanswered.

scene.name: Dance Floor
scene.description: The music turns the argument without ending it.

segments.text: Miss Ivors presses your hand in the chain. For a moment accusation and friendship occupy the same gesture.

segments.speaker: Miss Ivors
segments.text: Then you will think of it.

choices.text: Bow as the figure ends.

scene.name: Window Embrasure
scene.description: The glass is cold under your tapping fingers.

segments.speaker: Gretta
segments.text: O, do go, Gabriel. I'd love to see Galway again.
The west has crossed from Miss Ivors' mouth into your wife's.

choices.text: Say coldly that she can go if she likes.
Ask whether she misses it.

scene.name: Window Embrasure
scene.description: Beyond the window the park and the monument are only imagined whiteness.

segments.text: Irish hospitality. Sad memories. The Three Graces. Paris. The quotation.
Miss Ivors will not be sorry to see you fail. Or perhaps she has already forgotten you.

choices.text: Insert a small barb against the new generation.
Keep the speech for your aunts, not for Miss Ivors.

scene.name: Drawing Room
scene.description: Aunt Julia stands by the piano, no longer smiling, her voice pitched into the room.

segments.text: Her voice attacks the old air with a strength her face does not promise. Without looking at her, one could believe in swift flight.
When the applause comes, colour struggles into her face.

choices.text: Applaud loudly with the others.
Notice only how old she looks after the song.

scene.name: Drawing Room
scene.description: The applause has scarcely settled before old grievances find room.

segments.speaker: Aunt Kate
segments.text: There is such a thing as common everyday politeness and gratitude.
The room smiles and shifts. Julia's song remains in it, but already as something past.

choices.text: Help Mary Jane turn everyone toward supper.
Let Kate's anger have its dignity before the table claims you.

scene.name: Supper Room
scene.description: Goose, ham, spiced beef, jellies, almonds, raisins, bottles, knives and orders crowd the table.
scene.arrival: Aunt Kate finds you at last and sets you at the head.

segments.text: The carver sits well in your hand. For the first time tonight, a task fits you exactly.

choices.text: Carve with easy good humour.
Serve everyone and keep none for yourself.

scene.name: Supper Room
scene.description: The table noise is warm enough to bury almost any subject.

segments.text: Opera names pass over the plates. Then monks, silence, two in the morning, coffins.

segments.speaker: Mary Jane
segments.text: The coffin is to remind them of their last end.

choices.text: Let the lugubrious subject die in the tablecloth.
Make a little joke before silence can settle.

scene.name: Supper Room
scene.description: The glasses are filled. The three hostesses look down at the cloth.

segments.text: A few gentlemen pat the table. You push back your chair and lean ten trembling fingers on the cloth.

choices.text: Begin with the old formula of gratitude.
Feel the room turn upward to you and nearly sit down again.

scene.name: Supper Room
scene.description: Beyond the door the piano is playing a waltz tune.

segments.text: The words come. Hospitality, absent faces, living duties, the Three Graces of the Dublin musical world.
They laugh at the right place. Aunt Kate takes out her handkerchief.

choices.text: Let the toast close warmly.
Let the sentence about the new generation cut a little deeper.

scene.name: Supper Room
scene.description: The song rises from the table, fork and glass and voice joined for a moment.

segments.text: All the guests turn toward the three ladies. Freddy beats time with a pudding-fork.
The evening has accepted your words. That should have been enough.

choices.text: Join the last chorus and let the house have its triumph.

scene.name: Morkan House Hall
scene.description: The morning air enters the hall; coats, jokes and farewells overlap.
scene.arrival: The party is breaking into parcels and directions.

segments.text: Mr Browne laughs at the doorstep. Freddy has found only one cab. Your aunts advise everyone at once.
Then you see Gretta near the top of the first flight.

choices.text: Look up and hold the others quiet.
Attend to the cab arrangements instead.

scene.name: Morkan House Hall
scene.description: The door closes and at last the sound from above becomes audible.

segments.text: Only when the laughter thins do you hear the uncertain notes of a man's voice. Gretta is still on the stairs.

choices.text: Now look at her.

scene.name: Staircase
scene.description: The gaslight leaves Gretta half in shadow. The song is upstairs and far away.
scene.arrival: She leans on the banisters as if she were listening for someone outside the house.

segments.text: If you were a painter, you would paint her so. Distant Music, you would call it.

segments.speaker: D'Arcy
segments.text: O, the rain falls on my heavy locks...

choices.text: Ask for silence until the air is gone.
Let Mary Jane hurry upstairs to capture the singer.

scene.name: Morkan House Hall
scene.description: Scarves are tied; Mr D'Arcy swathes his throat with wounded pride.

segments.speaker: Gretta
segments.text: What is the name of that song you were singing?

segments.speaker: D'Arcy
segments.text: The Lass of Aughrim.

choices.text: Watch Gretta's eyes as she repeats the title.
Think only that the night is turning romantic.

scene.name: The Quay
scene.description: Slush lies underfoot. The lamps burn redly in the murky air.

segments.text: Gretta walks before you with Mr D'Arcy, her shoes in a brown parcel, her skirt lifted from the slush.
Your old tenderness returns with a new heat. You want to be alone with her.

choices.text: Store the image of her on the stairs like a painting.
Think of the hotel room and hurry the party onward.
Ask her at once what the song was to her.

scene.name: The Quay
scene.description: The river and the street take the question without answering it.

segments.speaker: Gretta
segments.text: Not here, Gabriel.
She does not say it harshly. That makes it harder to answer.

choices.text: Let the cab's rattle save you from more words.

scene.name: Cab Across the City
scene.description: The old horse drags the rattling box under the heavy morning sky.

segments.text: Conversation breaks into small remarks about streets and buildings. Gretta looks out of the window and seems tired.
Snow lies on the statue when you cross the bridge.

choices.text: Make the joke and wave good-night to Dan.
Say nothing and watch the snow on stone.

scene.name: Hotel Stairs
scene.description: The porter carries a guttering candle. The carpet takes the sound of your feet.
scene.arrival: Gretta climbs ahead with her head bowed.

segments.text: The wax falls into the tray. Your heart answers it in your ribs.

choices.text: Hold yourself still until the porter opens the room.
Let impatience show in your voice.

scene.name: Hotel Room
scene.description: Street light lies in a long shaft from the window to the door. The mirror waits in it.
scene.arrival: You send the porter away with his candle.

segments.text: Gretta stands before the swinging mirror, unhooking her waist. When you say her name, she turns with a face so serious and weary that your words fail.

choices.text: Ask only whether she is tired.
Try to draw her back by talking of Freddy Malins.
Leave the room rather than stand inside her silence.

scene.name: Hotel Corridor
scene.description: The carpet gives back no sound. The door behind you is almost closed.

segments.text: You tell yourself she is tired, that morning makes nonsense of all moods, that the song was only a song.
In the room behind you a woman is left with a memory you have chosen not to hear.

choices.text: Keep walking.

scene.name: Hotel Room
scene.description: The street lamp keeps the room half public, half secret.

segments.text: You speak of Freddy's pound, of decency, of small matters that cannot account for the room.
Then Gretta crosses to you and kisses you lightly.

segments.speaker: Gretta
segments.text: You are a very generous person, Gabriel.

choices.text: Ask what she is thinking about.
Hold the kiss as proof and press nearer.

scene.name: Hotel Room
scene.description: The mirror shows too much of the room and not enough of her.

segments.speaker: Gretta
segments.text: O, I am thinking about that song, The Lass of Aughrim.
She breaks from you and hides her face against the bed-rail.

choices.text: Ask who once sang it.
Ask whether she was in love with him.
Say she need not tell you.

scene.name: Hotel Room
scene.description: The bed-rail receives her tears. The window receives the snowlight.

segments.text: For a time she says nothing. You have been kind, perhaps. You have also left a door closed.

choices.text: Sit beside the closed story.
Ask again, gently.

scene.name: Hotel Room Window
scene.description: Gretta grows quiet. The window keeps its pale square of street light.
scene.arrival: You sit where the story might have opened.

segments.text: You have spared her another telling, or spared yourself the hearing of it. The difference is hard to name while she breathes unevenly into the quilt.
At the window, snow begins again with the patience of something that does not need to be invited.

scene.name: Hotel Room
scene.description: The room has narrowed to her voice.

segments.speaker: Gretta
segments.text: It was a young boy I used to know in Galway, named Michael Furey.
The name stands in the room with you.

choices.text: Ask coldly whether that was why she wished to go to Galway.
Ask what became of him.

scene.name: Hotel Room
scene.description: The street lamp makes the window a pale square beside her grief.

segments.speaker: Gretta
segments.text: He is dead. He died when he was only seventeen.
Your irony fails before the dead boy in the gasworks.

choices.text: Let jealousy speak once more.
Ask, more humbly, what he died of.

scene.name: Nuns' Island
scene.description: A wet window, a back garden, a wall, a tree at the end of it.
scene.arrival: Gretta's voice carries the room westward.

segments.speaker: Gretta
segments.text: I think he died for me.
She tells you of gravel at the window, rain on the glass, the delicate boy standing in the garden and saying he did not want to live.
Afterward she sobs into the quilt until the story is no longer speech.

choices.text: Hold her hand until the story finishes.
Withdraw into the humiliation of being compared.

scene.name: Hotel Room Window
scene.description: Gretta sleeps. A boot lies on its side. A petticoat string touches the floor.
scene.arrival: You walk quietly to the window.

segments.text: She had had that romance in her life. A man had died for her sake.
Aunt Julia, too, will soon be a shade. One by one they are all becoming shades.

ending_true_snow.title: Faintly Falling
ending_true_snow.description: You lie down beside Gretta without waking her. The room has grown cold around your shoulders. In the dark you see, or nearly see, a young man under a dripping tree, and beyond him other forms, wayward and flickering, who had once made the solid world.
ending_true_snow.closing: Snow falls softly through the universe, upon all the living and the dead.

ending_branch_jealous.title: The Warm Room
ending_branch_jealous.description: You keep your back to the window. The boy from Galway remains a rival because that is easier than letting him become dead. Gretta sleeps, spent by a grief you have already begun to call excessive.
ending_branch_jealous.closing: The room stays warm. Outside it, snow goes on without you.

ending_normal_glass.title: Glass Between
ending_normal_glass.description: You watch the pane brighten and darken with the falling snow. You have heard enough to know that the life beside you is not wholly yours, but not enough to follow where the knowledge leads.
ending_normal_glass.closing: The flakes touch the glass and vanish there.

ending_branch_west.title: Westward
ending_branch_west.description: In your mind the city gives way to darker ground: the plain, the Shannon waves, the hill where the boy is buried. It is not forgiveness and not defeat. It is the beginning of knowing that the west has been in the room all evening.
ending_branch_west.closing: By morning, the journey has already started.

ending_special_voice.title: A Voice Under Rain
ending_special_voice.description: Because you listened before you desired, the song returns less as accusation than as weather. Michael Furey is not only a boy who died for her. He is a voice carried through rain, through Gretta, through the old house, through Julia's fading song.
ending_special_voice.closing: For a moment, all music is made by the dead and lent to the living.

ending_rash_door.title: The Door Left Open
ending_rash_door.description: You leave before the dance can receive you. Behind the door the old women recover themselves, Gretta is folded into the upstairs laughter, and your name becomes a difficulty politely stepped around.
ending_rash_door.closing: The snow has a large country to cover, and you have made yourself small in it.

ending_rash_laughter.title: Bad Form
ending_rash_laughter.description: Freddy is not sober, but neither is he the only fragile thing in the house. Your severity spreads faster than drunkenness. The young ladies remember the silence; Aunt Kate remembers who caused it.
ending_rash_laughter.closing: A good evening can survive much, but not a man proud of being right.

ending_rash_table.title: No Toast
ending_rash_table.description: The table waits for the customary words and receives your refusal instead. Someone laughs too late. Mary Jane covers the gap; Aunt Kate thanks the company with trembling cheer.
ending_rash_table.closing: Without the toast, even the food seems to have been served in error.

ending_rash_corridor.title: The Corridor
ending_rash_corridor.description: You walk until the corridor turns and the room is no longer visible. By morning you will return with a reason: fatigue, wine, the lateness of the hour. Reasons are easy things.
ending_rash_corridor.closing: The story remains behind the door, and still it ages there.
